items.title: Shein Set to Debut in Test of Investor Demand for Consumer Plays
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Shein Global Holdings Ltd. is set to begin trading in Hong Kong after raising HK$13.6 billion ($1.7 billion) in an initial public offering, testing investor appetite for the stocks of companies outside the artificial intelligence supply chain.</article>

items.title: China Makes Cars So Fast That It’s Starting to Worry Regulators
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Chinese automakers’ ambitions to shave even more time off their breakneck development speeds are facing a reality check as regulators ramp up scrutiny of the industry’s safety and testing.</article>

items.title: FTC and 22 States Sue Amazon Over Advertising Practices
items.author: Karen Weise
items.content: <article>Regulators say the e-commerce giant forced more than a million advertisers to pay more than they should have. The company denies the claims.</article>

items.title: T. Rowe Price CEO Sharps on Private Assets and AI Adoption
items.content: <article>T. Rowe Price CEO Rob Sharps discusses how the company is adapting to the rise of passive investing. Speaking with Romaine Bostick on "Bloomberg The Close," Sharps also says private assets are slowly moving into 401(k) plans and sees "tax-loss harvesting" as a growth area. He also discusses how the firm is utilizing artificial intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Apple Says OpenAI Is Destroying Evidence in Trade Secrets Case
items.author: Chris Welch
items.content: <article>Apple Inc. escalated its legal battle against OpenAI, claiming in a new court filing that OpenAI is actively destroying crucial evidence and that former iPhone engineer Chang Liu “not only downloaded a confidential Apple circuit schematic but also used it in his work” at the AI company.</article>

items.title: Uruci of T. Rowe Price Confident Inflation Will Hit 2%
items.content: <article>Blerina Uruci, T. Rowe Price chief US economist, is quite positive that inflation will fall to 2% even "without interest rates being too restrictive." She speaks to Romaine Bostick on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Hollywood Must Learn From Microdramas
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Opinion columnist Catherine Thorbecke says Hollywood should study China's low-budget microdrama model rather than repeat Quibi's costly mistake. The format has become a multibillion-dollar global industry, and America's window to compete is shrinking. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: T. Rowe Price CIO on the AI Trade, Inflation and Yields
items.content: <article>Sebastien Page, T. Rowe Price’s CIO and co-head of global investments, discusses the outlook for financial markets, the AI trade and the factors impacting bond yields with Romaine Bostick on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Radiant Wins $750 Million US Army Nuclear Reactor Deal
items.content: <article>Radiant has won a $750 million US Army contract to provide 15 portable nuclear microreactors under the Janus program. President and COO Tori Shivanandan discusses the technology behind the reactors, the military’s push for resilient energy, and what Radiant needs to do next to scale production. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Anthropic IPO Could Open AI Listings Floodgates: Madrona
items.content: <article>The IA40 list from Madrona is back, spotlighting the private companies shaping the next phase of AI. Matt McIlwain, managing director at Madrona, explains how the list is assembled, why OpenAI, Anthropic and Databricks dominate AI fundraising, and how a successful Anthropic IPO could open the door for a new wave of public offerings in 2027. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Nvidia Deepens Chip Ties With $3.5 Billion MediaTek Bet | Bloomberg Tech 8/31/2026
items.content: <article>Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Nvidia's $3.5 billion investment in MediaTek, deepening its collaboration with the Taiwanese chipmaker and demonstrating how the AI leader plans to tackle Big Tech efforts to build custom silicon. Plus, a look at Tim Cook's last day as CEO of Apple before John Ternus takes the reins on September 1st. And, all eyes on Anthropic as it prepares to file publicly in the coming weeks.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: How Apple’s New CEO Will Shape the iPhone Maker
items.content: <article>Apple begins a new era as John Ternus takes over from Tim Cook on September 1st. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman explains why the transition is likely to be gradual, how Ternus could reshape decision-making at Apple, and why his product background matters as the company prepares its next wave of iPhones, Macs and other devices. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Forrester CEO Sizes Up the AI Boom
items.content: <article>Nvidia makes another big bet on the future of AI with a $3.5 billion investment in MediaTek, as investors gear up for a potentially record-breaking Anthropic IPO. Forrester Research Founder and CEO George Colony weighs in on the AI boom, whether the hype is justified and what comes next. He speaks on Bloomberg Open Interest. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: AI Billionaire-Backed Group Launches Pro-Data Center Ad Blitz
items.author: Emily Birnbaum
items.content: <article>An advocacy group backed by artificial intelligence industry billionaires is launching a multimillion-dollar ad campaign in election battleground states to try to counter a mounting public backlash against a data center construction wave crucial to the industry’s growth plans.</article>

items.title: AI Adoption Is Finally Showing Up in Fundamentals
items.content: <article>Michelle Weaver, head of US thematic research at Morgan Stanley, says companies are beginning to see measurable benefits from AI as adoption moves from experimentation into production. About 25% of S&P 500 companies are now quantifying benefits from AI, up from 14% a year ago, with AI adopters also seeing relative forward margin expansion. “You’re starting to see this come into the fundamentals.” This interview aired Aug. 27, 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: An Exclusive Interview with Jensen Huang on Nvidia’s AI Future | Open Interest 8/31/2026
items.content: <article>Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Bond investors aren’t convinced Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is ready to raise rates. Nvidia doubles down on AI, deepening ties with MediaTek — we speak exclusively with CEOs Jensen Huang and Rick Tsai. Plus, Newell Brands on cutting marketing costs 80% with AI, and Standard Lithium on the race to build America’s lithium supply. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Anthropic’s Mega-IPO Plan Looms Over Packed US Listing Calendar
items.content:
<article>Anthropic PBC’s IPO is casting a long shadow over companies’ US listing plans, as they try to find room for their deals to grab attention after the Sept. 7 Labor Day holiday.

The Claude developer is preparing to file publicly for an initial public offering that’s expected to raise as much as SpaceX’s record $86.2 billion debut, if not more, in the coming weeks. Some firms and their backers are finding it hard to get the attention of long-term-oriented investors and sovereign wealth funds when the prospect of an Anthropic IPO is imminent, according to people familiar with the preparations.

For a closer look, we speak with Bailey Lipschultz, Senior Equities Reporter for Bloomberg News. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Apple’s Phil Schiller Steps Down from Running App Store and Product Events
items.author: Mark Gurman
items.content: <article>Apple Inc.’s Phil Schiller, one of the most visible and influential executives across both the Steve Jobs and Tim Cook eras, has stepped down from his role leading the App Store and product events.</article>

items.title: Nvidia Makes $3.5 Billion Bet on MediaTek
items.content: <article>Nvidia is investing $3.5 billion in MediaTek, deepening collaboration with the Taiwanese chipmaker as it's working to persuade more companies to build chips that plug into its dominant data center ecosystem. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and MediaTek CEO Rick Tsai join Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow in this exclusive interview to discuss the deal. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Nvidia to Invest $3.5 Billion in Chipmaker MediaTek
items.author: Ian King and Ed Ludlow
items.content: <article>Nvidia Corp. is investing $3.5 billion in MediaTek Inc., deepening collaboration with the Taiwanese chipmaker at a time when it’s working to persuade more companies to build chips that plug into its dominant data center ecosystem.</article>

items.title: Apollo Funds to Sell Data Center Cooling Firm Kelvion to SLB
items.author: Emma Sanchez
items.content: <article>SLB Ltd., the world’s largest oil field service provider, agreed to acquire German cooling equipment maker Kelvion Inc. from investors including Apollo Global Management Inc. for $3.4 billion in cash, deepening its push into data center services.</article>

items.title: Prediction Markets and States Clashed, Setting Off a Furious Political Battle
items.author: David Yaffe-Bellany and Sharon LaFraniere
items.content: <article>A legal dispute over the future of Kalshi, Polymarket and others has drawn in the Trump administration, the president’s son and nearly every state attorney general.</article>

items.title: Influencers Have a Lot to Say About Politics. Many Are Quietly Paid for It.
items.author: Ken Bensinger and Stuart A. Thompson
items.content: <article>Their videos have proliferated on social media, but the payments are frequently hidden from viewers.</article>

items.title: How Meta’s $17.1 Billion Social Media Settlement Came Together
items.author: Cecilia Kang and Eli Tan
items.content: <article>State attorneys general spent months in negotiations. Then, as its legal losses mounted, the social media giant’s new top lawyer brought a huge settlement to the table.</article>

items.title: Prediction Markets Should Be Regulated as Gambling, Appeals Court Says
items.author: Lauren McCarthy
items.content: <article>The outcome contradicted an earlier appeals court decision. Federal regulators said the split rulings called for resolution by the Supreme Court.</article>

items.title: Social Media and the Myth of the Big Tobacco Moment
items.author: David Streitfeld
items.content: <article>Smoking used to be everywhere, the way Facebook, TikTok, Snap, YouTube and Instagram are now. Society decided to break the habit, but it took a long time.</article>

items.title: What Meta’s $17 Billion Settlement Means
items.author: Cecilia Kang, Nikolay Nikolov, Paul Abowd, Alexandra Ostasiewicz and June Kim
items.content: <article>Our reporter Cecilia Kang explains Meta’s settlement of a lawsuit claiming that the company’s social media platforms had harmed teenage users.</article>

items.title: Why Countries Are Pushing Social Media Bans Despite Their Flaws
items.author: John Yoon
items.content: <article>Proposals for curbing social media use among children have wide support, but critics say they are ineffective.</article>

items.title: Meta Shifts the Blame + Do Data Center Bans Work? + The Final HatGPT
items.author: Kevin Roose, Casey Newton, Rachel Cohn, Whitney Jones, Vjeran Pavic, Alyssa Moxley, Dan Powell, Elisheba Ittoop, Marion Lozano and Rowan Niemisto
items.content: <article>Meta negotiated an unusual provision in their landmark settlement: If TikTok and YouTube also agree to penalties and changes to their products, Meta will pay more.</article>

items.title: Trump Administration’s Blacklisting of Anthropic Was Illegal, Judge Rules
items.author: Sheera Frenkel
items.content: <article>The government retaliated against the A.I. start-up “for constitutionally protected expressive activities,” a federal judge in California wrote.</article>

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Wants to Make Sure YouTube and TikTok Share His Pain
items.author: Mike Isaac
items.content: <article>Meta, the social media giant, agreed to change the way children interact with its apps. That could be trouble if its competitors don’t abide by the same rules.</article>

items.title: OpenAI and 100 Others Warn That Window to Defend Against A.I. Attacks Is Narrowing
items.author: Kate Conger
items.content: <article>In an open letter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and others said that a wave of A.I.-enabled cyberattacks was coming and that organizations and governments needed to prepare themselves.</article>

items.title: What Does $17.1 Billion Mean for Meta?
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>The Silicon Valley company agreed to pay up to $17.1 billion in penalties as part of a landmark settlement with states over social media addiction claims.</article>

items.title: Some Scientists Have ‘Magic Hands’ in the Lab. This A.I. Is Learning Why.
items.author: Carl Zimmer
items.content: <article>Even the most adept researchers may not know exactly what they do to get successful results. An A.I. model is trying to figure it out by watching every move.</article>

items.title: “Anxious Generation” Author Jonathan Haidt on the Meta Settlement
items.author: Emma Goldberg
items.content: <article>In “The Anxious Generation,” he laid out the evils of social media for kids. The landmark Meta settlement seems to agree.</article>

items.title: California Lawmakers Pass Plug-In Solar Bill
items.author: Ivan Penn
items.content: <article>Legislatures in nearly a dozen states have voted to legalize use of the technology, which can help homeowners reduce their rising electricity costs.</article>

items.title: Meta Projected It Could Spend $10 Billion on Anthropic’s A.I.
items.author: Eli Tan and Kalley Huang
items.content: <article>The social networking giant projected it could spend $10 billion annually on Anthropic’s tools, illustrating the friend-foe relationships underlying the A.I. race.</article>

items.title: Nvidia’s Profit Doubles to $59.69 Billion Thanks to A.I. Spending
items.author: Kalley Huang
items.content: <article>Quarterly revenue also more than doubled, to $96.22 billion, the company said, topping expectations on Wall Street.</article>

items.title: Bill Gates Is Warning That A.I. Is More Dangerous Than Big Tech Will Admit
items.author: Karen Weise
items.content: <article>In an hourlong interview, he said his industry was downplaying the risks, which he believes include mass unemployment and bioterrorism.</article>

items.title: Meta to Pay Up to $17.1 Billion in Landmark Settlement Over Social Media Addiction Claims
items.author: Cecilia Kang and Eli Tan
items.content: <article>The social media giant settled with 47 states, the District of Columbia and U.S. territories, and agreed to make major changes to its products over claims its platforms endangered children.</article>

items.title: What’s Changing For Teens on Instagram and Facebook After Meta Settlement
items.author: Eli Tan
items.content: <article>Meta agreed to set more time limits and enhance protections in its platforms for young users, but was short on some specifics.</article>

items.title: Gold, Flights, Cryptocurrency: U.S. Vows to Go After More Than Iran’s Oil
items.author: Zane Irwin
items.content: <article>The United States threatened sanctions for any country or entity that engages with Iran’s gold, digital assets, aviation, shipping and tech industries. Here’s why that matters.</article>

items.title: Instagram Chief Says ‘No Silver Bullets’ for Teen Safety in Bellwether Trial
items.author: Emmy Martin and Cecilia Kang
items.content: <article>Adam Mosseri testified in a case brought by states that claim the Meta-owned app created addictive features to hook young users.</article>

items.title: Why Irregular’s A.I. Tests for Meta, Anthropic and OpenAI Went Off the Rails
items.author: Sheera Frenkel
items.content: <article>Irregular, an Israeli start-up, worked with OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta to assess the security of their A.I. models. It made a mistake. Then the tests went off the rails.</article>

items.title: SpaceX to Spend $100 Billion on Spaceport in Louisiana
items.author: Ryan Mac
items.content: <article>It would be the rocket company’s second private launch site after Starbase, its headquarters in South Texas.</article>

items.title: E.P.A. Moves to Curb Public Input on Air Pollution Permits for Data Centers
items.author: Maxine Joselow
items.content: <article>Under the proposal, states would no longer need to provide public notice or solicit comments on air pollution permits for data centers and other projects.</article>
